title: MongoDB vs PostgreSQL?
content:
# MongoDB vs PostgreSQL (Document vs Relational)

| Dimension | PostgreSQL | MongoDB |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Data Model** | Relational tables with strict columns & types. | BSON (Binary JSON) documents with dynamic schema. |
| **Joins & Relations** | Native, highly optimized multi-table `JOIN`s. | Embedded subdocuments or `$lookup` aggregation. |
| **Transactions** | Full ACID standard across all tables & operations. | Multi-document ACID supported (since 4.0), best suited for single-document atomicity. |
| **Scaling** | Vertical scaling + Read Replicas (Citus for sharding). | Native horizontal sharding out of the box. |

title: Embedded documents vs references?
content:
# MongoDB Schema Design: Embedding vs Referencing

---

## 1. Embedded Documents (Denormalized)
```json
{
  "_id": "order_123",
  "customer": "Alice",
  "items": [
    { "name": "Laptop", "price": 1200 },
    { "name": "Mouse", "price": 40 }
  ]
}
```
- **When to Use:** 1-to-1 or 1-to-Few relationships where data is always read together.
- **Pros:** Single atomic disk read; no joins required.

---

## 2. Referencing (Normalized)
```json
{
  "_id": "order_123",
  "customerId": "cust_456"
}
```
- **When to Use:** 1-to-Many (1:10,000+) or Many-to-Many relationships to avoid hitting MongoDB's 16MB document size limit.
